1	# Resting
     2	[![Swift](https://github.com/rocxteady/Resting/actions/workflows/swift.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/rocxteady/Resting/actions/workflows/swift.yml)
     3	
     4	`Resting` is an async/await-first Swift package for common REST client work.
     5	It provides typed request definitions, validated HTTP responses, a shared typed
     6	error model, secondary Combine compatibility APIs, and per-operation download
     7	handles with isolated progress and cancellation.
     8	
     9	## Requirements
    10	
    11	- Swift 6.2
    12	- Apple platforms supported by `Package.swift`: iOS 15+, macOS 12+, watchOS 8+, tvOS 15+, visionOS 1+
    13	
    14	## Installation
    15	
    16	Add `Resting` to your Swift Package Manager dependencies:
    17	
    18	```swift
    19	dependencies: [
    20	    .package(url: "https://github.com/rocxteady/Resting.git", branch: "main")
    21	]
    22	```
    23	
    24	## Primary Async Flow
    25	
    26	Import the package and configure a client:
    27	
    28	```swift
    29	import Resting
    30	
    31	let configuration = RestClientConfiguration(
    32	    sessionConfiguration: .default,
    33	    decoder: JSONDecoder(),
    34	    encoder: JSONEncoder(),
    35	    defaultHeaders: ["Accept": "application/json"]
    36	)
    37	
    38	let client = RestClient(configuration: configuration)
    39	```
    40	
    41	Build a request with the request style that matches the operation:
    42	
    43	```swift
    44	let request = RequestDefinition.json(
    45	    url: URL(string: "https://api.example.com/articles")!,
    46	    method: .post,
    47	    body: CreateArticleRequest(title: "Modern API"),
    48	    headers: ["Authorization": "Bearer token"]
    49	)
    50	```
    51	
    52	Execute raw or decoded responses:
    53	
    54	```swift
    55	let rawPayload = try await client.execute(request)
    56	let rawData = rawPayload.value
    57	
    58	let article: Article = try await client.execute(
    59	    .query(url: URL(string: "https://api.example.com/articles/1")!),
    60	    as: Article.self
    61	)
    62	```
    63	
    64	## Request Styles
    65	
    66	Use the specialized constructors instead of a single overloaded request type:
    67	
    68	```swift
    69	let search = RequestDefinition.query(
    70	    url: URL(string: "https://api.example.com/articles")!,
    71	    queryItems: [URLQueryItem(name: "page", value: "1")]
    72	)
    73	
    74	let form = RequestDefinition.form(
    75	    url: URL(string: "https://api.example.com/login")!,
    76	    fields: ["email": "hello@example.com", "password": "secret"]
    77	)
    78	
    79	let json = RequestDefinition.json(
    80	    url: URL(string: "https://api.example.com/articles")!,
    81	    body: CreateArticleRequest(title: "Modern API")
    82	)
    83	
    84	let raw = RequestDefinition.raw(
    85	    url: URL(string: "https://api.example.com/upload")!,
    86	    body: Data("payload".utf8),
    87	    contentType: "application/octet-stream"
    88	)
    89	```
    90	
    91	## Combine Compatibility
    92	
    93	Combine remains available as a secondary surface when an app still needs
    94	publisher-based integration:
    95	
    96	```swift
    97	import Combine
    98	
    99	let cancellable = client
   100	    .publisher(for: request, as: Article.self)
   101	    .sink(
   102	        receiveCompletion: { completion in
   103	            if case .failure(let error) = completion {
   104	                print(error.localizedDescription)
   105	            }
   106	        },
   107	        receiveValue: { article in
   108	            print(article)
   109	        }
   110	    )
   111	```
   112	
   113	## Downloads, Progress, And Cancellation
   114	
   115	Each download returns its own `TransferHandle`, so overlapping transfers do not
   116	share hidden mutable client state:
   117	
   118	```swift
   119	let handle = client.download(
   120	    .download(url: URL(string: "https://example.com/archive.zip")!)
   121	)
   122	
   123	handle.observeProgress { progress in
   124	    print(progress.fractionCompleted)
   125	}
   126	
   127	let fileURL = try await handle.value
   128	```
   129	
   130	Cancellation is per handle:
   131	
   132	```swift
   133	handle.cancel()
   134	```
   135	
   136	## Error Handling
   137	
   138	All public execution paths use the same `RestingError` model:
   139	
   140	- `invalidRequest(reason:)`
   141	- `transport(URLError)`
   142	- `invalidResponse`
   143	- `statusCode(Int, Data?)`
   144	- `decoding(underlying:data:)`
   145	- `cancelled`
   146	- `fileSystem(underlying:)`
   147	
   148	Example:
   149	
   150	```swift
   151	do {
   152	    let article: Article = try await client.execute(request, as: Article.self)
   153	    print(article)
   154	} catch let error as RestingError {
   155	    switch error {
   156	    case .statusCode(let code, _):
   157	        print("Unexpected status:", code)
   158	    case .cancelled:
   159	        print("Cancelled")
   160	    default:
   161	        print(error.localizedDescription)
   162	    }
   163	}
   164	```
   165	
   166	## Migration Guide
   167	
   168	This release intentionally introduces source-breaking cleanup to remove the old
   169	flat API.
   170	
   171	- Replace `RequestConfiguration` with `RequestDefinition`.
   172	- Replace `fetch(with:)` with `execute(_:)`, `executeData(_:)`, or `execute(_:as:)`.
   173	- Replace ad hoc request payload overloads with `.query`, `.form`, `.json`, `.jsonData`, `.raw`, and `.download`.
   174	- Replace client-global `download(with:completion:progress:)` plus `cancel()` with per-operation `TransferHandle` instances.
   175	- Replace legacy `RestingError.urlMalformed`, `wrongParameterType`, and `unknown` handling with the richer typed error cases listed above.
   176	
   177	## Development Standards
   178	
   179	Project standards for contributors are tracked in `.specify/memory/constitution.md`.
   180	Public API changes are expected to include tests, docs, and localized
   181	user-facing strings where applicable.
   182

     1	# Resting
     2	[![Swift](https://github.com/rocxteady/Resting/actions/workflows/swift.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/rocxteady/Resting/actions/workflows/swift.yml)
     3	
     4	`Resting` is an async/await-first Swift package for common REST client work.
     5	It provides typed request definitions, validated HTTP responses, a shared typed
     6	error model, secondary Combine compatibility APIs, and per-operation download
     7	handles with isolated progress and cancellation.
     8	
     9	## Requirements
    10	
    11	- Swift 6.2
    12	- Apple platforms supported by `Package.swift`: iOS 15+, macOS 12+, watchOS 8+, tvOS 15+, visionOS 1+
    13	
    14	## Installation
    15	
    16	Add `Resting` to your Swift Package Manager dependencies:
    17	
    18	```swift
    19	dependencies: [
    20	    .package(url: "https://github.com/rocxteady/Resting.git", branch: "main")
    21	]
    22	```
    23	
    24	## Primary Async Flow
    25	
    26	Import the package and configure a client:
    27	
    28	```swift
    29	import Resting
    30	
    31	let configuration = RestClientConfiguration(
    32	    sessionConfiguration: .default,
    33	    decoder: JSONDecoder(),
    34	    encoder: JSONEncoder(),
    35	    defaultHeaders: ["Accept": "application/json"]
    36	)
    37	
    38	let client = RestClient(configuration: configuration)
    39	```
    40	
    41	Build a request with the request style that matches the operation:
    42	
    43	```swift
    44	let request = RequestDefinition.json(
    45	    url: URL(string: "https://api.example.com/articles")!,
    46	    method: .post,
    47	    body: CreateArticleRequest(title: "Modern API"),
    48	    headers: ["Authorization": "Bearer token"]
    49	)
    50	```
    51	
    52	Execute raw or decoded responses:
    53	
    54	```swift
    55	let rawPayload = try await client.execute(request)
    56	let rawData = rawPayload.value
    57	
    58	let article: Article = try await client.execute(
    59	    .query(url: URL(string: "https://api.example.com/articles/1")!),
    60	    as: Article.self
    61	)
    62	```
    63	
    64	## Request Styles
    65	
    66	Use the specialized constructors instead of a single overloaded request type:
    67	
    68	```swift
    69	let search = RequestDefinition.query(
    70	    url: URL(string: "https://api.example.com/articles")!,
    71	    queryItems: [URLQueryItem(name: "page", value: "1")]
    72	)
    73	
    74	let form = RequestDefinition.form(
    75	    url: URL(string: "https://api.example.com/login")!,
    76	    fields: ["email": "hello@example.com", "password": "secret"]
    77	)
    78	
    79	let json = RequestDefinition.json(
    80	    url: URL(string: "https://api.example.com/articles")!,
    81	    body: CreateArticleRequest(title: "Modern API")
    82	)
    83	
    84	let raw = RequestDefinition.raw(
    85	    url: URL(string: "https://api.example.com/upload")!,
    86	    body: Data("payload".utf8),
    87	    contentType: "application/octet-stream"
    88	)
    89	```
    90	
    91	## Combine Compatibility
    92	
    93	Combine remains available as a secondary surface when an app still needs
    94	publisher-based integration:
    95	
    96	```swift
    97	import Combine
    98	
    99	let cancellable = client
   100	    .publisher(for: request, as: Article.self)
   101	    .sink(
   102	        receiveCompletion: { completion in
   103	            if case .failure(let error) = completion {
   104	                print(error.localizedDescription)
   105	            }
   106	        },
   107	        receiveValue: { article in
   108	            print(article)
   109	        }
   110	    )
   111	```
   112	
   113	## Downloads, Progress, And Cancellation
   114	
   115	Each download returns its own `TransferHandle`, so overlapping transfers do not
   116	share hidden mutable client state:
   117	
   118	```swift
   119	let handle = client.download(
   120	    .download(url: URL(string: "https://example.com/archive.zip")!)
   121	)
   122	
   123	handle.observeProgress { progress in
   124	    print(progress.fractionCompleted)
   125	}
   126	
   127	let fileURL = try await handle.value
   128	```
   129	
   130	Cancellation is per handle:
   131	
   132	```swift
   133	handle.cancel()
   134	```
   135	
   136	## Error Handling
   137	
   138	All public execution paths use the same `RestingError` model:
   139	
   140	- `invalidRequest(reason:)`
   141	- `transport(URLError)`
   142	- `invalidResponse`
   143	- `statusCode(Int, Data?)`
   144	- `decoding(underlying:data:)`
   145	- `cancelled`
   146	- `fileSystem(underlying:)`
   147	
   148	Example:
   149	
   150	```swift
   151	do {
   152	    let article: Article = try await client.execute(request, as: Article.self)
   153	    print(article)
   154	} catch let error as RestingError {
   155	    switch error {
   156	    case .statusCode(let code, _):
   157	        print("Unexpected status:", code)
   158	    case .cancelled:
   159	        print("Cancelled")
   160	    default:
   161	        print(error.localizedDescription)
   162	    }
   163	}
   164	```
   165	
   166	## Migration Guide
   167	
   168	This release intentionally introduces source-breaking cleanup to remove the old
   169	flat API.
   170	
   171	- Replace `RequestConfiguration` with `RequestDefinition`.
   172	- Replace `fetch(with:)` with `execute(_:)`, `executeData(_:)`, or `execute(_:as:)`.
   173	- Replace ad hoc request payload overloads with `.query`, `.form`, `.json`, `.jsonData`, `.raw`, and `.download`.
   174	- Replace client-global `download(with:completion:progress:)` plus `cancel()` with per-operation `TransferHandle` instances.
   175	- Replace legacy `RestingError.urlMalformed`, `wrongParameterType`, and `unknown` handling with the richer typed error cases listed above.
   176	
   177	## Development Standards
   178	
   179	Project standards for contributors are tracked in `.specify/memory/constitution.md`.
   180	Public API changes are expected to include tests, docs, and localized
   181	user-facing strings where applicable.
   182

---
name: speckit-git-commit
description: Auto-commit changes after a Spec Kit command completes
compatibility: Requires spec-kit project structure with .specify/ directory
metadata:
  author: github-spec-kit
  source: git:commands/speckit.git.commit.md
---

# Auto-Commit Changes

Automatically stage and commit all changes after a Spec Kit command completes.

## Behavior

This command is invoked as a hook after (or before) core commands. It:

1. Determines the event name from the hook context (e.g., if invoked as an `after_specify` hook, the event is `after_specify`; if `before_plan`, the event is `before_plan`)
2. Checks `.specify/extensions/git/git-config.yml` for the `auto_commit` section
3. Looks up the specific event key to see if auto-commit is enabled
4. Falls back to `auto_commit.default` if no event-specific key exists
5. Uses the per-command `message` if configured, otherwise a default message
6. If enabled and there are uncommitted changes, runs `git add .` + `git commit`

## Execution

Determine the event name from the hook that triggered this command, then run the script:

- **Bash**: `.specify/extensions/git/scripts/bash/auto-commit.sh <event_name>`
- **PowerShell**: `.specify/extensions/git/scripts/powershell/auto-commit.ps1 <event_name>`

Replace `<event_name>` with the actual hook event (e.g., `after_specify`, `before_plan`, `after_implement`).

## Configuration

In `.specify/extensions/git/git-config.yml`:

```yaml
auto_commit:
  default: false          # Global toggle — set true to enable for all commands
  after_specify:
    enabled: true          # Override per-command
    message: "[Spec Kit] Add specification"
  after_plan:
    enabled: false
    message: "[Spec Kit] Add implementation plan"
```

## Graceful Degradation

- If Git is not available or the current directory is not a repository: skips with a warning
- If no config file exists: skips (disabled by default)
- If no changes to commit: skips with a message
